name: PROSPECT
aliases: PROlapse Surgery: Pragmatic Evaluation and randomised Controlled Trials
question: Does adding a synthetic mesh inlay or biological graft to a primary transvaginal anterior or posterior prolapse repair improve patient-reported prolapse symptoms over native-tissue repair?

design.blinding: Participants, ward staff and outcome assessors masked where possible; surgeons not masked

arms.label: Standard repair with a polypropylene mesh inlay
standard repair with a biological graft inlay

design.population: Women at 35 UK hospitals undergoing primary transvaginal anterior or posterior compartment prolapse repair.
design.description: Two pragmatic multicenter parallel-group randomized trials, surgeons unmasked
design.locator: PDF pp1,3-4 and Figure (trial profile) footnotes; mesh and graft trials share the 545-woman standard-repair group (1,348 analyzed of 1,352 randomized)

verdictNote: Neither augmentation improved POP-SS at 1 year; 12% of mesh recipients had a mesh complication by 2 years
takeaway: Adding a polypropylene mesh inlay or a biological graft to primary transvaginal anterior or posterior prolapse repair did not improve 1-year Pelvic Organ Prolapse Symptom Scores versus native-tissue repair alone; 51 of 434 women who received synthetic mesh had a mesh complication within 2 years.

reports.label: 2-year randomized report
reports.citation: Glazener CMA, Breeman S, Elders A, et al. Mesh, graft, or standard repair for women having primary transvaginal anterior or posterior compartment prolapse surgery: two parallel-group, multicentre, randomised, controlled trials (PROSPECT). *Lancet.* 2017;389(10067):381-392.
reports.followUp: 1-year primary outcomes and clinic review; questionnaires to 2 years (79% to 82% of each arm returned the 24-month questionnaire)

results.measure: 1-year Pelvic Organ Prolapse Symptom Score (0 to 28; lower is better), mesh trial; mean difference (mesh minus standard)
results.note: Prespecified minimally important difference 2 points; the 95% CI excludes it. Positive differences favor standard repair.

results.measure: 1-year POP-SS, graft trial; mean difference (graft minus standard)
results.note: The standard-repair comparison group of the graft trial overlaps the mesh trial's (stratum A, 252 women).

results.measure: 1-year prolapse-related quality-of-life visual analogue score (0 to 10; lower is better), mesh trial; mean difference
1-year prolapse-related quality-of-life score, graft trial; mean difference
2-year POP-SS, mesh trial; mean difference (mesh minus standard)
results.note: The report lists primary outcomes as measured at 1 and 2 years; the 1-year POP-SS was the primary clinical outcome.

results.measure: 2-year POP-SS, graft trial; mean difference (graft minus standard)
1-year POP-Q leading edge beyond the hymen (stage 2b, 3 or 4), mesh trial; risk ratio (mesh versus standard)
results.note: Higher proportion with objective failure in the mesh arm was not statistically significant.

results.measure: 1-year POP-Q leading edge beyond the hymen (stage 2b, 3 or 4), graft trial; risk ratio (graft versus standard)
1-year at least one prolapse symptom (POP-SS above 0), mesh trial; risk ratio
1-year at least one prolapse symptom (POP-SS above 0), graft trial; risk ratio
New prolapse operation in the first year after surgery, mesh trial; risk ratio
New prolapse operation in the first year, graft trial; risk ratio
New prolapse operation in the second year, mesh trial; risk ratio
results.note: Operations in the same or another compartment; 6% of women overall had a new prolapse operation within 2 years.

results.measure: New prolapse operation in the second year, graft trial; risk ratio
1-year International Consultation on Incontinence vaginal symptoms score (higher is worse), graft trial; mean difference
results.note: Confidence intervals were not adjusted for multiple comparisons; the mesh-trial score did not differ (7.2 versus 7.5; P=0.38).

results.measure: 2-year any report of 'something coming down', graft trial; risk ratio
results.note: Unadjusted for multiple comparisons; the mesh-trial comparison at 2 years did not differ (106/347 [31%] versus 116/342 [34%]; P=0.59).

harms.label: Serious adverse events in year 1, excluding mesh complications
harms.note: Risk ratio 1.08 (95% CI 0.68 to 1.72; P=0.73) for mesh and 1.57 (0.95 to 2.59; P=0.08) for graft. Serious events were infection, urinary retention, dyspareunia or other pain, and other events meeting the trial's definition.

harms.label: Mesh complications, year 1
harms.note: Mesh complications in the standard-repair and graft arms followed synthetic mesh that surgeons used for the repair or a concomitant procedure.

harms.label: Mesh complications, year 2 (new in that year)
Surgical removal or oversewing of mesh, year 1
harms.note: In the mesh trial 25 women had partial mesh removal in the first year (2 in the standard arm); 18 (72%) were asymptomatic and 16 (64%) had exposures under 1 cm2. One woman had total mesh removal within 2 weeks for severe infection.

harms.label: Surgical removal or oversewing of mesh, year 2 (new in that year)
harms.note: Of the 17 mesh-trial women, 13 (76%) were asymptomatic and 10 (59%) had exposures under 1 cm2.

harms.label: Mesh complication within 2 years among women who received synthetic mesh by any route
harms.note: Includes mesh given as a concomitant vault, uterine or continence procedure; 37 of the 51 had surgical removal. Restricted to mesh used only as the anterior or posterior repair: 41/284 (14%). Treatment was conservative in about a third.

harms.label: Severe dyspareunia at 1 year
harms.note: Adjusted risk ratio 1.73 (95% CI 0.52 to 5.78) for mesh and 1.17 (0.43 to 3.23) for graft. Denominators as printed in the table.

delivery.label: Received the allocated repair, by arm
delivery.locator: PDF p4, Figure (trial profile); p7 text
delivery.note: Denominators are women who had surgery. In the mesh arm 60 (14%) had standard repair; in the graft arm 57 (16%) had standard repair. Reasons for non-compliance were in the appendix.

delivery.label: Women randomized, analyzed and operated
delivery.value: 1,352 randomized (55% of 2,478 eligible); 1,348 analyzed; 23 had no surgery and contributed baseline data only
delivery.note: Mesh trial 865 (430 standard, 435 mesh); graft trial 735 (367 standard, 368 graft); 252 stratum A women with standard repair were in both trials.

delivery.label: Materials used
delivery.value: Type 1 monofilament macroporous polypropylene inlays (19 to 44 g/m2; hybrid coated mesh allowed); porcine acellular collagen, porcine small intestinal submucosa or bovine dermis grafts
delivery.note: Surgeons chose any available product and used their usual technique, with midline or fascial plication permitted; graft or mesh was placed below the fascial layer when possible and secured with peripheral sutures.

delivery.label: Operator
delivery.value: Consultants or doctors with completed specialty training did 78% and 81% of procedures in the standard and mesh arms of the mesh trial and 69% and 75% in the standard and graft arms of the graft trial

delivery.label: Primary outcome data available at 1 year
delivery.value: 784/865 (91%) in the mesh trial; 679/735 (92%) in the graft trial

delivery.label: Examiners masked for 1-year POP-Q
delivery.value: 581/657 (88%) in the mesh trial; 539/573 (94%) in the graft trial

reports.label: Complications, all 2,632 operated women
reports.citation: Reid FM, Elders A, Breeman S, et al. How common are complications following polypropylene mesh, biological xenograft and native tissue surgery for pelvic organ prolapse? A secondary analysis from the PROSPECT trial. *BJOG.* 2021;128(13):2180-2189.
reports.followUp: 2 years after surgery; analysis by treatment received (1,712 native tissue, 482 mesh inlay, 360 xenograft, 78 mesh kit)

results.measure: De novo severe dyspareunia at 24 months by repair received
results.note: Mesh kit 4.8%. Descriptive analysis by treatment received; no inferential comparisons. Severe dyspareunia overall at 24 months: 4.8% native tissue, 3.4% mesh inlay, 4.2% xenograft, 13.0% mesh kit.

results.measure: De novo vaginal tightness at 24 months by repair received

harms.label: Mesh exposure and removal among women who received mesh
harms.note: Mesh exposure in 12.0% of women who received mesh, 64.2% of those exposures asymptomatic; surgical removal of mesh in 7.9% (95% CI 5.5 to 11.1%), extent of removal not recorded.

harms.label: Bladder and bowel injury, all procedures
harms.note: Bladder injury 0.4% (1 in 263; 95% CI 0.2 to 0.7%); bowel injury 0.2% (1 in 526; 95% CI 0.1 to 0.4%).

harms.label: Prolonged catheterization over 10 days, all procedures
harms.note: 3.9% (95% CI 3.2 to 4.7%), more common in the mesh kit group.

harms.label: De novo urinary incontinence at 24 months, all procedures
Readmission for non-mesh complications over 2 years, all procedures
harms.note: 4.3% (95% CI 3.5 to 5.1%); most common causes were vaginal adhesions, urinary retention, infection and constipation.

harms.label: Infection, all procedures
harms.note: 2.4% (95% CI 1.9 to 3.1%); infection with abscess 0.1% (95% CI 0.01 to 0.3%).

harms.label: De novo extreme generic pain or discomfort at 24 months
harms.note: 3.0% (95% CI 2.3 to 3.8%) overall; none after mesh kit. Extreme pain or discomfort at baseline in 8.4%, improved after surgery in all groups.

delivery.label: Population
delivery.value: 2,632 women who had a transvaginal anterior or posterior repair, randomized or in the comprehensive cohort, primary or repeat repair
delivery.note: Within the randomized trials, xenograft was not used for recurrent prolapse and mesh kits were not used for primary repairs.

reports.label: 4- and 6-year follow-up
reports.citation: Reid FM, Aucott L, Glazener CMA, et al. PROSPECT: 4- and 6-year follow-up of a randomised trial of surgery for vaginal prolapse. *Int Urogynecol J.* 2023;34(1):67-78.
reports.followUp: 4 and 6 years by postal questionnaire; 72% of randomized women retained at 4 years and 65% at 6 years

results.measure: 6-year POP-SS, mesh trial; mean difference (mesh minus native tissue)
results.note: Questionnaire only; no examination at 4 or 6 years.

results.measure: 6-year POP-SS, graft trial; mean difference (graft minus native tissue)
6-year functional cure (no sense of something coming down, no prolapse surgery, no pessary), mesh trial; risk ratio
6-year functional cure, graft trial; risk ratio
4-year POP-SS, mesh trial; mean difference (mesh minus native tissue)
results.note: Below the prespecified minimally important difference of 2 points.

results.measure: 4-year POP-SS, graft trial; mean difference (graft minus native tissue)
Cumulative new prolapse operation within 6 years, mesh trial; risk ratio
Cumulative new prolapse operation within 6 years, graft trial; risk ratio
6-year completely satisfied with surgery, mesh trial
results.note: Ordinal-regression effect printed as 1.67 (95% CI 1.31 to 2.13) without a stated direction; 8.6% were fairly dissatisfied and 8.6% very dissatisfied after mesh versus 3.1% and 5.8% after native tissue.

results.measure: 6-year completely satisfied with surgery, graft trial

harms.label: Mesh removed within 6 years (cumulative)
harms.note: Risk ratio 5.24 (95% CI 1.84 to 14.96; P=0.002) for mesh versus native tissue. Mesh removal in the native-tissue and graft arms followed mesh placed at another operation.

harms.label: Severe dyspareunia at 6 years
harms.note: Risk ratio 1.88 (95% CI 0.69 to 5.10) for mesh and 0.91 (0.18 to 4.57) for graft; denominators as printed in the table.

harms.label: Extreme pain or discomfort (EQ-5D-3L) at 6 years
harms.note: Mesh trial; risk ratio 0.60 (95% CI 0.25 to 1.45; P=0.255). The graft-trial row is not reproduced because the table prints no denominator for the graft arm.

harms.label: Severe urinary incontinence at 6 years
harms.note: Risk ratio 1.58 (95% CI 0.97 to 2.59; P=0.067) for mesh and 1.36 (0.73 to 2.52) for graft.

delivery.label: Examination-based anatomy at 4 and 6 years
delivery.value: Not collected; examination planned for 12 years

delivery.label: Randomized women retained for the primary outcome
delivery.note: 23 did not consent to contact for long-term follow-up and 42 withdrew consent for further questionnaires.
